title: [recoverability][observability] A drill row says how its newest drill went (part 1 of 105/105b: the API and the north star): each Core lines drills row carries its newest drill's own result, and a row whose newest drill failed is not counted in the north star
prompt:
Read crates/spawn-cli/src/serve/core_lines/drills.rs (the recovery rows of the Core lines file: a row's last pass, the north star `recoverability.restores_passed`), NEWEST_PASSED in crates/spawn-postgres/src/host.rs, and drillMark in web/src/coreLines.ts (the Home card's drill rows).

The problem (lead, 11-13; made visible by 104, which gives the transcript archive and the mission repositories drill records). A drill row carries only its last pass: for a `record` row the newest record of its type with ok true, for a `unit` row the unit's last success. So a drill that failed yesterday after passing two days ago still reads as passed for up to 7 days, the north star counts it, and nothing on the card says it failed: a user sees a resource as restorable while its newest restore failed.

Required behaviour.
- Each `drills` row of GET /api/core-lines gains `last`: its newest drill's own result, {at_ms, ok, reason}, or null without one (no drill; a record type with no record; a unit that has not run). A `record` row: the newest control record of that type whatever its ok: at_ms its time, ok true exactly when its `ok` is JSON true, reason its `reason` when that is a string, else "". A `unit` row: the unit's last run, from the same `systemctl show` the pass is read from (no other call): ok exactly when Result is success and ExecMainStatus 0, at_ms its ExecMainExitTimestamp (null when it has none), reason "" when ok, else "Result=<Result>, ExecMainStatus=<status>". `passed_at_ms` and `source` are unchanged.
- The north star `recoverability.restores_passed` counts a row only when its last pass is within 7 days and its newest drill did not fail (`last` null or ok true). The two ages are unchanged.
- The card is 105b's (part 2, after this one lands): this objective changes no web file.

Polled-read cost (the lead's rule): Core lines is read on every Home poll. A `record` row's two facts, its last pass and its newest drill, come from one statement per record type (rev-g N1), replacing NEWEST_PASSED for these rows: the newest control record of the type, and only when that one did not pass, the newest passing one (a subplan in the CASE branch not taken does not run). So a row whose newest drill passed costs one lookup, a failed one two, and each type is read once per reading however many rows name it. Newest means by recorded time, the id breaking a tie (NEWEST_PASSED is ordered the same way in this objective): the column order of rev-f's index for control records of a type ((type), recorded_at_ms, id), so each lookup is one backward index read (rev-g); without it, a backward read of the control stream (54 ms per type live for a type with no record). So this is assigned after rev-f's interventions fix. A `unit` row adds no call: its last run comes from the same kept `systemctl show` reading. Standalone read-only SELECT for the live timing ($1 each record type of ws/core-lines.json; time it for a type whose newest passed and one whose newest failed):
  explain (analyze, buffers)
  with newest as (
    select e.recorded_at_ms as at_ms, e.kind -> 'detail' -> 'record' as record
      from spawn_events e
     where e.session_id = 'session_control' and e.event_name = 'control.recorded'
       and e.kind -> 'detail' -> 'record' ->> 'type' = 'backup.verified'
     order by e.recorded_at_ms desc, e.id desc limit 1)
  select jsonb_build_object('at_ms', n.at_ms, 'record', n.record,
    'passed_at_ms', case when n.record -> 'ok' = 'true'::jsonb then n.at_ms
                         else (select e.recorded_at_ms from spawn_events e
                                where e.session_id = 'session_control' and e.event_name = 'control.recorded'
                                  and e.kind -> 'detail' -> 'record' ->> 'type' = 'backup.verified'
                                  and e.kind -> 'detail' -> 'record' -> 'ok' = 'true'::jsonb
                                order by e.recorded_at_ms desc, e.id desc limit 1) end)
    from newest n;

Files (expected; no other open objective touches them; after rev-f's interventions fix, which carries the index): crates/spawn-cli/src/serve/core_lines/drills.rs (the rows, `last`, the north star; its unit tests), crates/spawn-postgres/src/host.rs (DRILL_OF_TYPE: a record type's newest record and last pass in one statement). Not schema.sql, core_lines.rs, the records' writers (102, 104 and rev-f's) or any web file (105b's). About 260 changed lines with the unit tests; one more crate than the web part, which is split off as 105b (the lead, 11-13).

Acceptance: rsi/scenarios/105.sh. On its own database, with seeded control records and a fake systemctl: Database (backup.verified) passed 3 h ago and failed 1 h ago; Transcript archive (backup.drilled.transcripts) passed 5 h ago; Mission repositories no record; Session files (unit) passed 10 h ago; Off-host copy (unit) failed 10 h ago; Old drill (unit) passed 8 days ago; Configuration and credentials no drill. (1) Each row's `last` is as above, and the reading calls systemctl once per unit row; (2) the north star reads 2 (093's rule gave 3: the failed Database row counted). 100, 086, 090, 095, check-web and check-schema-upgrade must still pass, and 093 with its (2) as this contract changes it: 093's history has a database drill that passed 3 h ago and failed 1 h ago, so its north star is 1 (the session files), not 2; the contract's push changes that expectation (093.sh (2) and its header), and 093 then fails on main until 105 lands.
